txt: A smirk crosses her face as she watches you stand there, mute. Then she exhales sharply, shakes her head, and pulls the trigger.
She chuckles. "*Tribunal* is an awfully fancy word for what they're going to do. But, yeah, I was listening to their frequency. They've finished their 'investigation.'"
She eyes you warily, as though gauging your sincerity.
She flashes you an incredulous grin. Then she exhales sharply, shakes her head, and pulls the trigger.
She frowns. "She had some pretty messed up people after her. She's going to come out of that meat grinder a different person... If she comes out at all."
She looks at the machine, assessing the damage. Her hand trembles.
She looks at you incredulously. "What is this? I thought Titus and I had a decent collegial relationship..."
She looks at you incredulously. "What? I don't even understand what you're trying to get at here."
She looks you in the eye impassively, making it clear that she's not planning to comment on the matter any further.
She narrows her eyes. "That sound about right?"
She pauses, taking it in. "Well, fuck. And those guys *liked* me -- I know it. If this is what happens to people whom people like..."
She pulls the trigger before you finish your sentence.
She raises her eyebrows. "Nope."
She rolls her eyes again. "If that's what she wants on the record, so be it. I'm not about to go into details for you to jerk off to later."
She runs past you, then past the lieutenant, and disappears into the darkness of the tunnel.
She scoffs. "Can't do either without some power of mind over bladder. And, anyway, that wouldn't have been enough time."
She scoffs. "That's your prerogative."
She sighs. "Yeah. The mercenaries are about to set up a tribunal and execute someone for killing Lely."
She smiles bitterly. "Nah, she didn't crack. She's a survivor. If she told you anything, it was to save herself..."
She stares at you, frozen, the gun still in her mouth, eyes filled with dark intensity. Then something shifts in her.
Suddenly, your entire body is paralysed. Aggressive white noise fills your skull -- a strange pain like you've never felt before. The static overcomes you.
Suddenly, your entire body is paralysed. Aggressive white noise fills your skull -- a strange pain like you've never felt before. Through the static, you hear a woman's voice.
The woman runs past you and disappears into the darkness of the tunnel.
You watch as her brains trickle out through her neon hair.
You're overwhelmed with a new surge of violent static. It feels like a blood vessel exploded in your brain.
"*My* boys?"
"*Saw my equations*?" She snorts. "You've been sniffing through my lorry, right? I expected as much. I *am* a bit surprised you knew what you were looking at..."
"...for the same reason that she's everyone's type as an object of desire, she's not irreplaceable."
"...how the fuck do the rest of you get by?"
"...the shot couldn't have come from the roof. Or we would have all heard it downstairs."
"...war?" She purses her lips. "The thought crossed my mind. But the mercenary's death was going to have repercussions either way. Although, the way things are going..."
"A Nachtwey 80 front-loader. Two-barrelled -- not really what you were looking for, I'm guessing."
"A pale latitude compressor is used to sort of... make the pale more manageable. With a lot of these, you can force a radio signal grid on the pale -- literally crunch the distance across it."
"Ah, fuck it." She puts the barrel of the gun into her mouth.
"Alright, don't kill yourself over it. I was shooting the shit with Hardie and the boys over a few beers, like always. Then Klaasje comes in, all pale and shuddering..."
"And potentially bring attention to herself? No. Besides, the shot was made from a distance -- otherwise we would have heard it downstairs."
"And that topic was what? Staircases? Ladders?"
"And you -- watch out for yourselves. You seem to have a habit of walking into traps."
"And?"
"As I said -- watch out." She nods.

"At the upper limit is the large prime number generator station. It's used specifically for pale latitude compression. That's why you may be hearing some numbers. But you might also hear -- or think you're hearing -- local radio chatter."
"Aw, fuck. Took some convincing my ass. And those guys *liked* me -- I know it. If this is what happens to people whom people like..."
"Based on what I've heard about you -- you *are* serious scum," she responds, holding your gaze.
"But Klaasje couldn't have known I was here. How did you?"
"But she couldn't have known I was on the coast. How did you find me?"
"Can't say it's a pleasure, officer. I was really hoping *not* to make your acquaintance. But -- here we are. "
"Cool, man, cool. I'm glad you got off on it --  what the *fuck* are we talking about?"
"Cool. They sent a ghost-cop after me. Congratulations."
"Damn. That girl's pretty, but not *that* pretty. In fact, no one's pretty enough to waste time skulking about the Whirling, drilling holes in walls..."
"Day of miracles..." she says, pulling the gun out of her mouth, eyes still fixed on you. Then she turns her gaze to the tunnel behind you. "I'll take it."

"Don't know anything about it. No one's been around since I set up camp. But I'm sure I'm not the first vagabond to..." Her voice trails off into white noise in your head. It feels like an aneurysm approaching.
"Don't know it. But also..." She frowns, studying your face.

"Drugs don't make people abuse them; hopelessness does. As for the drug trade -- it would continue with or without me. I like to think that my efficiency as an organizer has at least prevented some internal conflicts."
"Eh, fuck it." She shrugs. "I'm not responsible for these people after what they did to me."
"Everyone in Jamrock. The cops, the criminals... Why do you think I'm holed up in here with a goddamn death ray, waiting for you?"
"Fantastic. I've gotta get on the road -- then you can go find your friends... Unless you have anything *pressing* to ask me."
"Fine, if you really want to talk, I can dial it down. I've also got a gun, by the way." She steps reluctantly out of the shadows. The pain lessens.
"Fine. I can dial it down. I've also got a gun, by the way." She steps reluctantly out of the shadows. The pain lessens.
"Glad to have been of assistance." She tosses her head back defiantly and turns down the machine. "Best of luck to you, officers -- Revachol's a bitch."
"Go ahead -- it's your body."
"Goddamnit." She regards you and Kim with sudden sympathy.
"Harry Du Bois," she replies quickly. "One corrupt motherfucker with the disco pants and the funny tie. Agent to La Puta Madre."
"He was still warm, but the blueish light coming through the broken window made him look as though he'd been dead for a good long while..."
"How should I know? As I keep saying, he already had a bullet in his head when I got to him, and there hasn't been any useful gossip over the radio..."
"I built it myself." She nods toward her torture device.
"I considered her a good friend, yeah."
"I did, didn't I. And now you've come for me." She scoffs. "But fuck them all the same."
"I didn't like him. Hardened mercenaries aren't particularly likeable types."

"I got lucky being a dispatcher -- never had to do any of the *really* dirty work myself. This gun," she glances at it, "has only been used for self-defence against serious scum." She turns the knob down just a millimetre.
"I heard you in the passages. And I've been preparing for quite a while."
"I knew that wasn't the whole story, but thought, fine, I'll take it and move on."
"I know it's bad -- try not to move."
"I know you're feeling pretty uncomfortable right now. Don't move too much or fight it. That'll just make it worse," says the shadowy figure by the machine.
"I never did understand why, when someone dies, a hothouse's worth of flowers has to die too."
"I really don't care which one of us you think was more at fault for the 'lynching.' Neither of us killed him, though."
"I saw *you* roll into town. I wasn't about to stick around for questioning by a goddamn La Puta Madre agent."
"I was a little worried she'd blow it out of proportion in her head -- all the drugs she was doing can make you feel like you're living in a Dolorian tragedy."
"I was listening in on their frequency." She pauses, biting her lip. "Even though those assholes gave me up... I'm worried for the boys."
"I was. Before I caught you in the pale latitude compressor. I'm fine now."
"I'm asking myself that right now too. Anyway, I'm guessing you don't know that a third mercenary has come to town just in time for the tribunal -- now you do."
"I'm guessing you don't know that a third mercenary has come to town just in time for the tribunal -- now you do."
"I'm listening."
"I'm not following your clever insinuations, detective."
"I'm not really into old shit for old shit's sake."
"I'm sad to hear that. The girl was playing some dangerous games, but even with what she did to me... I wouldn't have wished *that* upon her."
"I'm sure La Puta Madre himself will explain it all to you soon enough."
"I'm using a pale latitude compressor. You and your partner have been caught in its field."
"I've faced worse." She shrugs.
"If I want to stare at a pretty girl, I can pick one up at a bar -- or, worst case scenario, look at a naughty photo. Who has time to go skulking about the Whirling, drilling *holes* in walls?"
"If you've got something *really* important to say, you can do it through the white noise."
"Is that a joke or a threat? I'm guessing both."
"It's very powerful. I used it to tune into RCM frequencies. That's how I knew to be prepared for your arrival."
"Like *fuck* I did. I was *in* all the time -- I went for a leak, ten, fifteen minutes max."
"Like what?" She adjusts her grip on her gun. "I already told you I didn't do it."
"Look, I know this isn't very fun for you, so let's wrap this up. You have a tribunal to attend."
"Look, I'm not aware of any hole in Klaasje's wall. And if I had been, I would have told her to get it sealed -- that's what friends do."
"Look, fuck you, man. I might have also stopped by the bar."
"Man, I was with the boys the whole night. I hope they at least bothered to impress *that* upon you."
"Man, it's to get *away* from all that murderous shit that I left Jamrock -- my previous employer -- for the Union."
"Man, it's to get *away* from all that murderous shit that I left the Madre for the Union."
"My type? She's everyone's type. She's *your* type. Are you sure you're not the one who was excited about the peephole?"
"Nah. That I'm not planning to shoot you is the extent of the courtesy I can extend to La Puta Madre at present."
"Never really got into weapons trafficking. Especially not old weapons -- they break too often, and you don't want unhappy customers among gun collectors."
"No -- once I shut down the compressor, the pain will end." She hesitates. "It may take a few minutes for you to steady yourself, though -- it's a bit like waking out of a very confusing dream."
"No, I did not."
"No, I didn't do it. I only helped stage the lynching. Though I doubt that makes much of a difference to *you*."
"No, I really didn't. She's not that easy to read. I just assumed she'd done too much blow. It wouldn't be a first for her. But -- no such luck. She was in some *deep* shit."
"No, I'm not going to fucking kill you. If that had been my plan, you'd be dead already. All things considered, I'm being pretty reasonable here."
"No, gifts of flowers and candy aren't really my style."
"No, not since I was 14 and hanging out at the only diner in Dardanne. Haven't been into low-risk, no-reward games since moving to the city."
"No, they're not practical. Break too often."
"No."

"Nope. Look, she has an *effect* on people -- or had, before you sent her off in your Moralintern meat grinder. It's impossible not to look at her when she walks into the room -- and very difficult to look away. But -- travel enough, and you realize..."

"Nope. Look, she has an *effect* on people. That je ne sais quoi that makes it impossible not to look at her when she walks into the room -- and very difficult to look away. But -- travel enough, and you realize..."
"Not anymore, no. This could've turned out pretty bad for me if you hadn't walked right into 25 bands of ultra-high frequencies."
"Not for a moment do I believe that *you* came here unarmed."
"Not murder mysteries, either, if that's what you're thinking."
"Not particularly."
"Now they're going to put on a show before meting out punishment." She pauses, biting her lip. "Even though those assholes gave me up... I'm worried for the boys."
"Of you? No, not really."
"Oh yeah. *Super*. But I didn't think too much of it at first -- I'd seen her party hard before."
"Oh yeah. *Way* beyond." She studies her death ray and the law officials trapped in it.
"Oh yes, they do. The cops, the criminals... Why do you think I'm holed up in here with a goddamn death ray, waiting for you?"
"Oh, I wouldn't have wished that upon her... The girl was playing some dangerous games, but even with what she did to me... I wouldn't have wished *that* upon her."
"Oh, it doesn't even matter. How can they be *my* boys when they're not even my friends. And those guys *liked* me -- I know it. If this is what happens to people whom people like..."
"Oh, so that's where you were going with this." She shakes her head. "Do I *really* seem like someone who would do something as lame as committing murder out of jealousy?"
"Oh, so that's where you were going with this."
"Oh, yes, it is."
"Oh." She smiles sadly. "I knew the kitten had claws, but not like this..."
"Oh." She smiles sadly. "Well, I guess I always knew she was a *survivor* above all else."
"Okay, fine." She rolls her eyes. "I was into her. Klaasje was into me too, for a time, I know it -- we even fooled around once. And, yeah, after that I thought maybe we could make a go of it."
"Okay, great, you got into my lorry on your own. What now? You're going to arrest me for drug trafficking?" A bitter smile.
"One of the guys seemed chipper, a blond, the other had a brooding something-or-other about him... And the woman... the woman was the only one in uniform. All were carrying."
"Plenty of broken people who don't come with that kind of body count. Besides, they're paid well for what they do."
"Precisely. This is an industrial-strength paraboloid. It's meant for forcing dimensions on something that doesn't *have* them. Needless to say, the frequencies used are... out of this world."
"Problem-solving," she mutters.
"Proximity to the Pale Compressor is overloading his mind. He'll be okay once it's off, though."
"Really now? Check this out!" She turns the dial in her hand.
"Right, sure. You don't know."
"She asked me to come upstairs -- the merc she'd been going with was lying on the bedroom floor, dead. I knew she couldn't get the authorities involved. So, yeah..."
"She asked me to help her drag him into the shower so she could wind the shower head around his neck. To fake lividity. Then she dressed him while I went to get the Hardie boys."
"She does know how to pick 'em."
"She rejected me with some wishy-washy bullshit about how she was confused because she felt so close to me and valued my friendship so much, and how guilty she felt for leading me on..."
"She sits down with a drink, trying to steady her nerves. So I grab a seat next to her."

"Signals are relayed across a series of repeater stations fixed to buoys." She pauses. "Not a fun job, manning those stations. All alone out there in the pale, people lose their minds in just a few years."
"So nice." She smiles a little smile. "That's one knife I didn't want to find in my back."
"So now I'm leaving Revolutionary symbols around... Come on."
"So you found my shack, huh? I'm not surprised."
"So, heart-of-gold Tommy fucked me over too..." She shakes her head, slowly. "Never trust a musician."
"Sure don't."
"Sure you do, I bet they're just outside, waiting." She looks into the tunnel behind you. "I guess I'll take my chances."
"That boy's really gotta learn to keep his trap shut. And it's not a bloody pale emitter. It doesn't emit *pale*..."
"That's a very sentimental way of putting it. We both had *pasts* we didn't want to catch up with us. And we enjoyed listening to music together. Why not go on a road trip?"
"The fuck do elevators have to do with anything?"
"The gun store."
"The pale? It's the end of the world."
"The shot was made from a distance -- otherwise we would have heard it downstairs. Besides, she had good reason to not draw attention to herself."
"The view's pretty bomb too, but you might say the antenna was the main attraction there, yeah. Along with Klaasje."
"There, there, I told you it's best not to move."
"This could've turned out pretty bad for me if you hadn't walked right into 25 bands of ultra-high frequencies."
"Trigger-Happy Jack's."
"Well, it wasn't this scrawny dude." She nods toward the lieutenant. "You had two guys and a lady. The guys looked pretty buff. Lady wasn't bad either."
"Well, this has been a great talk, really. But I think I'm going to hit the road now."
"What are you doing? I told you -- it's best not to move..."
"What bunker?"
"What did you think? That I'm going to squeal on my gun supplier? Sorry, I'm not that kind of gal."
"What shit?" She adjusts her grip on her gun. "I told you I didn't do it. Sounds pretty simple to me."
"What the fuck, man? She's everyone's type. She's *your* type. Are you sure you're not the one who was excited about the peephole?"
"What the hell, man?!" She laughs. "Yeah, why not? I've gotten worse."
"What? No. Faking a lynching was her idea."
"Who doesn't? Oh, you probably mean Klaasje's rooftop. Sure, I've hung out there. She's got this great antenna..."
"Who hasn't?" She shrugs. "You know, I can still see him there, in Klaasje's room, lying on his side."
"Who ratted me out, by the way? Was it Titus? No," she hesitates, "he wouldn't have broken first..."
"Why are *you* so hung up on elevators?"
"Why?"
"Wow, check out the big brains on you." She sounds impressed. "You're not entirely wrong..."
"Wow, now I'm curious. Please, explain."
"Wow. Pissing, pinball, and now peeping. I'm just not following your insinuations, detective."
"Yeah, *really*?"
"Yeah, I stuck my head in there before using it on you. It seemed like the *ethical* thing to do. Can't say that I enjoyed it. The field was weaker, but I can imagine what you're going through."
"Yeah, I wasn't sure whether to admire her -- or be disturbed."
"Yeah, and I'm sure they also made some FUNNY remarks about it -- they always do. I've driven a lot of long haul and chugged a lot of beer, man."
"Yeah, and probably some ghosts from the time of the Suzerain. I'm not really interested in supranatural mysteries."
"Yeah, let's not talk about *that* shit. You were hunting me and fell into my trap instead. That's all there is to say about it."
"Yeah, one time when we'd both been drinking, I said some heated things about how dangerous her patterns with men were."
"Yeah, sure, and I didn't like Wild Pines sending in those foreign hirelings -- me and a fuck-ton of other people around here."
"Yeah, sure."
"Yeah, that figures." She shrugs. "What now? You're going to arrest me for drug trafficking?"
"Yeah, they love sending people to faraway places..."
"Yeah. *Evidence*."
"Yeah. In cold blood. It really surprised me -- how quickly she was able to get a hold of herself once we got up there. It was like she was another person. The *party girl* was gone."
"Yeah. Other questions."
"Yeah. The girl seemed terrified. The merc was beyond caring what happened to his mortal coil. It was a no-brainer."
"Yeah. You had your death squad with you. What happened to them, anyway?"
"Yeah? What?"
"Yeah? Where?"
"Yes -- you." She looks at you quizzically. "Everyone says you're his peone. His 'Human Can Opener.'"
"Yes, I'm sure. And, anyway, as I said before, the shot had to have come from afar."
"Yes, I'm sure." She pauses. "In fact, the shot couldn't have possibly come from the roof -- otherwise we would have heard it downstairs."
"You know what I did. I fucked him over." She pauses. "And now I have Harry Can-Opener in my lair. Fucking Titus..."
"You know who he is -- he fucked me over. Country boy my ass..."
"You mean, the length of a toilet break? That wouldn't even have been enough time."
"You think I was envious of his conquests? Look, pussy's not a problem for me. And definitely not a reason to off someone."
"You won't get to. Your dirty little tricks won't work with me," she responds, holding your gaze.
"You're big boys, you can handle it. Stop being so damned melodramatic."
